name: Daryl Mills
life: “My best customer buys nothing twice because everything can be resewn.” Sunday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Daryl prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I'm stitching a sunshade for a neighbor who will never set foot on a boat again.
appearance: Daryl has short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat, a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, and a favorite piece of clothing, a soft blue checked shirt. It usually goes with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. When somebody else has the floor, Daryl counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Daryl talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Daryl's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To install a shade where a frightened former sailor can use it.
family: Mona Brandt is Daryl’s cousin. Daryl remembers the birthdays. Mona asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The million-dollar flat*, Mona says, “I deliver her lunch. I love the joke about a millionaire buying soup on tick but I wish she'd let me balance the account.”
connections: Gloria Smith. A shorebound neighbor can keep a piece of water as a shade or a passport square.

reactions.situation: Two makers want the same piece of sail
reactions.response: Daryl lays both paper patterns on the piece before anybody cuts.

reactions.situation: A witness is embarrassed about remembering only a little
reactions.response: Daryl asks where they stood and what they could hear, leaving the rest open instead of filling it with guesses.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Daryl says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
